> **Note:** The `linechart()` function is designed primarily for use within **jamovi's GUI** (`JJStatsPlot` -> `Lines` -> `Line Chart`). The executable R examples below demonstrate every option, statistical table, assumption check, and jamovi Notice reproducibly.

# Line Chart (`linechart`)

## Overview

`linechart` creates time-series and longitudinal line charts for clinicopathological and clinical research, combining:

- **Observed trajectories** (`points`, `smooth` LOESS curves, `confidence` 95% bands, and `showRefline` clinical thresholds — including `refline = 0` for change-from-baseline or log fold-change).
- **Trend & association statistics** (`trendline = TRUE`): Pearson *r* with Fisher-*z* 95% confidence intervals, Spearman rank correlation (disclosing exact vs asymptotic inference for ties and *N* >= 1,290), OLS regression slope and *R*-squared, copy-ready APA/SAMPL reporting sentences, per-group stratified trends when `groupby` is set, and one-way ANOVA (*F* with degrees of freedom) for categorical X-axis visits.
- **Assumption diagnostics & native jamovi Notices**: nested polynomial partial *F*-test for linearity, Spearman $|e|$ constant-variance check, Shapiro-Wilk residual normality check (with explicit *n* > 5,000 guidance), and priority-ordered single-line `jmvcore::Notice` banners for missing/infinite exclusions, small sample sizes, repeated-X independence cautions, and confidence-band model-fit disclosure.
- **Accessible styling**: jamovi global theme (`theme = "jamovi"`) and palette integration, Okabe-Ito 8-color colorblind-safe palette (`colorPalette = "colorblind"`), Viridis, Tableau 10 (`"clinical"`), and high-contrast `publication` styling.

---

## 1. Basic Time-Series Line Chart

Using the bundled `linechart_simple` dataset:

```{r basic-linechart}
data("linechart_simple", package = "ClinicoPath")
head(linechart_simple)

res_basic <- linechart(
  data = linechart_simple,
  xvar = "time_point",
  yvar = "value"
)

res_basic$summary$asDF
```

```{r basic-plot, fig.cap="Basic longitudinal line chart with default data points."}
print(res_basic$plot)
```

---

## 2. Grouped Clinical Cohort with Trend Analysis & Stratified Per-Group Trends

When `groupby` and `trendline = TRUE` are both specified, `linechart` plots per-group lines and dashed OLS overlays, reports the overall pooled correlation (explicitly flagged for Simpson's-paradox risk), and adds **per-group stratified trend rows** (`Group Trend: <group> (Pearson r)`) so clinicians can compare within-arm trajectories directly.

```{r grouped-linechart}
data("linechart_grouped", package = "ClinicoPath")

res_grouped <- linechart(
  data = linechart_grouped,
  xvar = "time_point",
  yvar = "lab_value",
  groupby = "treatment",
  confidence = TRUE,
  trendline = TRUE,
  colorPalette = "colorblind",
  theme = "publication"
)

res_grouped$summary$asDF
res_grouped$correlation$asDF[, c("measure", "value", "ci_lower", "ci_upper", "pvalue")]
```

```{r grouped-plot, fig.cap="Grouped line chart with Okabe-Ito colorblind-safe palette, 95% confidence ribbons, and per-group linear trend overlays."}
print(res_grouped$plot)
```

---

## 3. Clinical Reference Thresholds (Including Zero)

The `showRefline` switch decouples enabling the reference line from its numeric value, allowing clinical thresholds at `0` (such as zero change from baseline) as well as upper/lower limits of normal:

```{r clinical-refline}
data("linechart_clinical", package = "ClinicoPath")

res_ref <- linechart(
  data = linechart_clinical,
  xvar = "week",
  yvar = "tumor_marker",
  groupby = "disease_stage",
  showRefline = TRUE,
  refline = 100,
  reflineLabel = "Upper Limit of Normal",
  xlabel = "Follow-up Week",
  ylabel = "Serum Tumor Marker (U/mL)",
  title = "Tumor Marker Trajectory by Disease Stage",
  theme = "minimal"
)

print(res_ref$plot)
```

---

## 4. Categorical Visits (One-Way ANOVA) & LOESS Smoothing

When `xvar` is a factor (for example ordered clinic visits), `linechart` preserves factor ordering (reordering numeric-label factors numerically while keeping `ordered` class), connects single-group levels cleanly, and reports a one-way ANOVA *F*-statistic with degrees of freedom when `trendline = TRUE`.

```{r categorical-x}
set.seed(2026)
visit_df <- data.frame(
  visit = factor(
    rep(c("Baseline", "Month 3", "Month 6", "Month 12"), each = 12),
    levels = c("Baseline", "Month 3", "Month 6", "Month 12"),
    ordered = TRUE
  ),
  score = c(
    rnorm(12, 42, 6),
    rnorm(12, 50, 6),
    rnorm(12, 58, 6),
    rnorm(12, 64, 6)
  )
)

res_cat <- linechart(
  data = visit_df,
  xvar = "visit",
  yvar = "score",
  trendline = TRUE
)

res_cat$correlation$asDF[, c("measure", "value", "pvalue", "interpretation")]
```

For nonlinear continuous trajectories, enable `smooth = TRUE` (with optional `confidence = TRUE` so the shaded ribbon matches the LOESS curve):

```{r smooth-loess}
data("linechart_long", package = "ClinicoPath")

res_smooth <- linechart(
  data = linechart_long,
  xvar = "day",
  yvar = "seasonal_value",
  points = FALSE,
  smooth = TRUE,
  confidence = TRUE,
  colorPalette = "viridis",
  theme = "classic"
)

print(res_smooth$plot)
```

---

## 5. Data Quality Notices & Assumption Diagnostics

`linechart` surfaces actionable single-line `jmvcore::Notice` banners in priority order (`STRONG_WARNING` and `WARNING` at the top; `INFO` at the bottom):

```{r notices-demo}
d_warn <- data.frame(
  time = c(1, 2, 5, 10, NA, 12),
  biomarker = c(10, 14, 20, 32, 18, Inf)
)

res_warn <- linechart(
  data = d_warn,
  xvar = "time",
  yvar = "biomarker",
  trendline = TRUE,
  confidence = TRUE
)

notices <- Filter(function(item) inherits(item, "Notice"), res_warn$items)
data.frame(
  name = names(notices),
  content = vapply(notices, function(x) as.character(x$content), character(1)),
  row.names = NULL
)
```

---

## 6. Options & Results Reference

### Options (`.a.yaml`)

| Option | Type | Default | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `data` | `Data` | — | Input data frame |
| `xvar` | `Variable` | `NULL` | X-axis variable (numeric time/sequence or ordered factor) |
| `yvar` | `Variable` | `NULL` | Y-axis continuous numeric outcome |
| `groupby` | `Variable` | `NULL` | Optional grouping factor for multiple series and stratified trends |
| `points` | `Bool` | `TRUE` | Display individual data points |
| `smooth` | `Bool` | `FALSE` | Apply LOESS smoothing to series |
| `confidence` | `Bool` | `FALSE` | Display 95% confidence interval ribbon (LOESS when `smooth = TRUE`, linear fit otherwise) |
| `trendline` | `Bool` | `FALSE` | Add linear regression trend overlay, correlation/stratified trend table, and assumption checks |
| `showRefline` | `Bool` | `FALSE` | Enable horizontal clinical reference line |
| `refline` | `Number` | `0` | Reference line value (drawn when `showRefline = TRUE`, including `0`) |
| `reflineLabel` | `String` | `"Reference"` | Annotation label for the reference line |
| `colorPalette` | `List` | `"default"` | `"default"` (honors jamovi palette), `"colorblind"` (Okabe-Ito), `"viridis"`, `"clinical"` (Tableau 10) |
| `theme` | `List` | `"jamovi"` | `"jamovi"` (active jamovi theme), `"minimal"`, `"classic"`, `"publication"` |
| `xlabel`, `ylabel`, `title` | `String` | `""` | Custom axis labels and chart title |
| `width`, `height` | `Integer` | `800`, `600` | Plot width (300–1200 px) and height (300–1000 px) |

### Results (`.r.yaml`)

| Result ID | Type | Visibility | Description |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `todo` | `Html` | Empty state only | Onboarding Quick Start Guide when `xvar` or `yvar` is unset |
| `naturalSummary` | `Html` | `(xvar && yvar)` | Plain-language summary of dataset, groups, Y range, and trend |
| `summary` | `Table` | `(xvar && yvar)` | Observation count, unique X count, group counts/names, Y mean, median, SD, and range |
| `correlation` | `Table` | `(xvar && yvar && trendline)` | Pearson *r* (95% CI, *p*), *R*-squared, slope, Copy-Ready Summary, Spearman *r*, per-group stratified trends, ANOVA *F* (categorical X), and Statistical Validity caveat |
| `assumptions` | `Html` | `(xvar && yvar && trendline)` | Linearity (polynomial partial *F*-test), residual normality (Shapiro-Wilk with *n* <= 5,000 guard), homoscedasticity (Spearman $|e|$), and clinical interpretation guidelines |
| `plot` | `Image` | `(xvar && yvar)` | Line chart rendered from saved state (`requiresData: false`) |
